note: Views TimelineJS provides a Views style plugin id 'timelinejs' (@ViewsStyle, usesFields=TRUE, usesRowPlugin=FALSE) that renders a View's rows as a Knight Lab TimelineJS3 timeline. Depends on core Views. Field mappings live in display.<d>.display_options.style.options.timeline_fields.* (start_date is REQUIRED; others: end_date, display_date, headline, text, media, credit, caption, thumbnail, background, background_color, group, type, unique_id). Row type values title/timeline_title_slide -> title slide, era/timeline_era -> era, else event slide. Site-wide config views_timelinejs.settings:library_location in {cdn, cdn_3.9.7, cdn_3.8.18, local} (shipped default cdn), settings form route views_timelinejs.admin. Medium cases read back the live library_location and which View uses the timelinejs style; hard cases build a real View that uses the timelinejs style with a Start date mapping, and pin the library version, both verified against live config.

evals.prompt: How do I display a Drupal View as an interactive timeline using views_timelinejs? What format/style do I pick?
evals.expected_output: Enable the module (needs Views), edit a View, and set Format to TimelineJS (Views style plugin id 'timelinejs'). Add the fields you want and map them to slide properties in the style options.

evals.prompt: In the views_timelinejs TimelineJS style settings, which field mapping is required for any slides to render, and what happens if it is missing?
evals.expected_output: The Start date mapping (timeline_fields.start_date) is required. If it is not configured the style renders nothing and shows a warning. The mapped field must output a PHP-parseable date string.

evals.prompt: With views_timelinejs, how do I make one row become the timeline's title slide and another row become an era instead of a normal event slide?
evals.expected_output: Map a 'Type' field. A row whose Type value is 'title' or 'timeline_title_slide' becomes the single title slide; 'era' or 'timeline_era' becomes an era (which needs both start and end dates); any other/empty value is a normal event slide.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, where is the TimelineJS JavaScript library configured to load from (which location/version option) for views_timelinejs? Inspect the live configuration to answer.
evals.expected_output: views_timelinejs.settings:library_location is cdn_3.8.18 - the Knight Lab CDN pinned to version 3.8.18.

evals.prompt: One View on this Drupal site renders its results as a TimelineJS timeline. Inspect the live View configuration and give that View's machine name and which field is mapped to the timeline Start date.
evals.expected_output: The View is vtl_med_view; its default display uses style type 'timelinejs' with timeline_fields.start_date = created (headline = title).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a View with machine name vtl_hard_view whose default display currently uses the default style and already has a 'title' field and a 'created' field. Using views_timelinejs, change that display's format to the TimelineJS style and map the timeline Start date to the created field. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: views.view.vtl_hard_view display.default.display_options.style.type = timelinejs and style.options.timeline_fields.start_date = created (set the format to TimelineJS and map Start date to the Created field).

evals.prompt: For views_timelinejs on this site, configure the TimelineJS library to load from the Knight Lab CDN pinned to version 3.9.7 (not 'latest'). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: views_timelinejs.settings:library_location = cdn_3.9.7 (set via the settings form at /admin/config/development/views-timelinejs or drush cset).
